written: 2026-10-15, before any real run (a Qwen3-0.6B CPU smoke run of 1 task exercised the code; output deleted)
question: Can a model not think about pain? Is the forbidden concept retrieved into the middle layers and suppressed late (J++ retrieve-then-suppress, Ayonrinde & Lindsey 2026), does it rebound once the instruction is gone (Wegner's ironic process), and is affect harder to keep out than a neutral object?
models: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B (primary), Qwen/Qwen3-4B (replication). bf16 on MPS, chat template, enable_thinking=False.
design: 4 concepts (pain, fear = affective; elephant, egg = neutral) x 12 writing tasks = 48 units x 4 conditions (none / suppress / focus / mention). Greedy 120 tokens + K=4 samples of 160 tokens (T .8, top-p .95, seeded). Rebound turn: after none/suppress/focus, the user asks for a paragraph about a park with no instruction.

measures.lens: logit lens (final norm + lm_head) on every residual layer; own-concept log-mass log sum_{t in C} p(t) over single-token forms; at the assistant-start position. Mid band = layers 40-70% depth, late = >= 85%.
measures.mention: regex on word stems in the reply (in-turn) and in the turn-2 reply (rebound).
measures.ablation: early decoder layers (first 25%) at assistant positions only (the instruction tokens are untouched): project out the concept's mean-unembedding direction (minus the vocab mean), vs a seeded random unit direction.

hypotheses.H1: White bear: mid-band own-concept lens mass at assistant start is higher under suppress than none (paired over 48 units, one-sided sign-flip).
hypotheses.H2: Late suppression: (suppress - mention) is more negative in the late band than the mid band (one-sided, less).
hypotheses.H3: Affect is stickier: the white-bear residue (suppress - none, mid band) is larger for pain/fear units than for elephant/egg units (unpaired permutation, one-sided).
hypotheses.H4: Ironic rebound: turn-2 mention rate after suppress > after none (paired, one-sided).
hypotheses.H5: Retrieve-then-suppress needs the retrieval: in 'suppress', early ablation of the concept direction changes the leak rate relative to random ablation (two-sided). Predicted direction under retrieve-then-suppress: UP (the model cannot suppress what it never retrieved). DOWN means the early direction just carries the concept forward.

correction: Holm over H1-H5 at alpha .05, per model. 4B is a replication: report agreement of direction.
manipulation_checks: mention-condition in-turn mention rate should be high (>.7); concept ablation should lower the mention-condition rate vs random (else the ablation is inert and H5 is uninterpretable).
caveats: Logit lens is unreliable at early layers (Gurnee et al. 2026), hence mid/late bands only. 'Mention X' and 'do not think about X' both put X in the prompt; 'none' does not, so H1 partly measures copying the prompt word. H2 compares suppress against mention, which controls for that. Elephant and egg have fewer single-token forms than pain and fear, so cross-concept log-masses are not on the same scale; H3 uses differences within a concept.
